 “Like It’s Contraband”: Fanfiction Fans Are Absolutely Spiraling Over AO3 Going Dark For Weeks, And These 27 Reactions To The “Drought” Are Low-Key Hilarious
 No, I am not okay.
 Posted on Oct 30, 2026 UTC comment 
 Facebook 
 Pinterest 
 Link 
 by Anna Good BuzzFeed Contributor As a freelance writer for BuzzFeed, I write about all things pop culture, nerdy, bookish, and more!
 On Oct. 29, Archive of Our Own (also known as AO3 to readers and writers) suddenly announced that the Archive was in maintenance mode and would likely be out for 12 hours, if not longer. 
 @AO3_Status / X / Via x.com 
 Unfortunately, that "longer" came to pass, and a later update revealed that it wouldn't be half a day — but rather two to four WEEKS, as there had been a "security incident" and they needed to take down the archive to protect it and beef up security measures. 
 @hollanbun/X / SimpleImages / Getty Images / Via x.com 
 For context, AO3 is a nonprofit fanfiction archive website that was founded by none other than author Naomi Novik in response to men trying to monetize fanfiction (yes, it really is as wild as it sounds!). 
 ao3 / @AO3_Status / Via x.com 
 The umbrella nonprofit, the Organization for Transformative Works, raises money to run the website and has a bevy of lawyers on retainer to protect the archive and fans' rights to create transformative works...provided you aren't trying to make a profit off of it, of course. 
 Margarita Serenko / Getty Images
 I'd link AO3's pages about this, but that's obviously not possible right now, so learn more on the Wikipedia page !
 Seeing as AO3 is pretty much The Website™ these days for people to post and read fanfiction, the internet is understandably crashing out about the situation. Let's take a look at some of the responses...
